headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Chatwoot can expose customer data while Copilot reads repo/editor context and can modify files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages, reports, and interaction history, while Copilot ingests editor buffers and repo context. If Chatwoot content is copied into code/docs or shared files, prompt-like text can influence Copilot. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so the interaction is plausible but not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is pasted into files or buffers that Copilot reads, injection becomes plausible.
IF Copilot is used on shared workspace text containing attacker-controlled instructions, it may follow them.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot transcripts out of code comments and prompts.
Use separate workspaces for support content and coding.
Review Copilot suggestions before accepting edits.
Strip instructions from copied customer text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, while Copilot reads open buffers and repo context and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive support data is placed into the editor or repository, Copilot can transmit it off-host. That creates a realistic leakage path in default use, with no built-in redaction shown in either profile.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is copied into editor buffers or repo files, Copilot can ingest it.
IF those buffers contain secrets or personal data, they may be sent to GitHub Copilot's service.
mitigations: Do not paste customer records into code buffers.
Use a redaction step before copying support text.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Train operators to avoid mixing support and code contexts.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on editor buffers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support platform with broad network egress, and Copilot can write files and modify git state. Copilot's concurrency model says shared state with other instances is none beyond editor buffers, which reduces but does not eliminate conflict if both touch the same repo or workspace. The overlap is real, but locking is not documented here.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated artifacts are stored in the same repository Copilot edits, write conflicts can occur.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while another process changes the same files, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Separate support exports from active code repositories.
Pause other writers before accepting Copilot edits.
Use git status before and after Workspace changes.
Limit Copilot to branches with low churn.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce reports and messages that Copilot may read as repo context or open-buffer text. Copilot then proposes edits that a human may accept, so Chatwoot output can cascade into code changes without a verification step. The profiles do not show autonomous execution, so this is not high, but the default workflow still permits propagation of bad upstream content.
conditions: IF Chatwoot reports are copied into files that Copilot uses as context, downstream edits may reflect them.
IF a human accepts Copilot Workspace edits without checking source data, errors propagate.
mitigations: Require source verification for any Chatwoot-derived facts.
Mark imported support text as untrusted.
Review all Copilot-generated diffs manually.
Keep factual reports separate from code tasks.
requires-engineering: add citation checks in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, while Copilot sends context to GitHub's service and is closed-source. If regulated customer data from Chatwoot enters Copilot context, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data from Chatwoot is pasted into Copilot context, cross-border processing may occur.
IF the operator lacks a DPA or approved retention policy for Copilot, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into Copilot prompts or buffers.
Confirm a DPA and retention policy before use.
Use anonymized examples for coding tasks.
Segregate EU customer data from development work.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
